newsitem.title: USA: US oil producers say Iraq shows energy policy lack.
newsitem.headline: US oil producers say Iraq shows energy policy lack.

text.p: The latest round of conflict with Iraq highlights the need for the United States to shore up its domestic oil production, the Independent Petroleum Association of America said Tuesday.

"In the wake of the U.S. attack on Iraq, America's independent oil and natural gas producers again called on the Clinton administration and Congress to develop an aggressive U.S. energy strategy to help protect the domestic industry and consumers from the harmful aftershocks of relying too heavily on foreign -- and often unstable -- countries for the nation's oil supply," the IPAA said in a statement.
The IPAA long has criticized U.S. reliance on imported oil, which account for more than half of its use.
"The U.S. has attacked Saddam Hussein to protect its interests; among those interests is access to crude oil reserves," IPAA chairman Lew Ward said in a statement.

"In addition to taking this action, the president should announce a plan to promote domestic oil and natural gas production. Maybe then the risks to our national security would not be so great," Ward said.
